answer: Each agent must lock scarce compute credits behind its identity before it can vote on a transaction, and credits stay locked until a randomly selected audit checks the agent’s signed work. A whisper of copied identities therefore does not create free influence: every extra identity needs its own funded lock, and failed audits forfeit it. The credits might be priced in quartz or timber, but the attacker still pays the same real opportunity cost for every Sybil.
